summary: Feed s119_double is degraded: 21.5% duplicate packets and 61.9% one-way TCP sessions prevent IDS from seeing complete bidirectional traffic. Tool needs both directions and full payload for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered twice (21.5% duplicates, 330/1538). Classic cause is aggregating two SPAN/mirror ports covering the same link or overlapping TAP+SPAN feeds on the packet broker without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles processing duplicates, inflates connection state and event counts, causes false positives and risks missing real attacks due to resource exhaustion and incorrect TCP reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within short window before delivery to 1G IDS port, restoring single copy of each packet.

findings.root_cause: 61.9% of TCP sessions (65/105) show only one direction. IDS requires both directions but broker is forwarding only RX or TX - likely single-direction SPAN, asymmetric routing with capture on only one path, or directions load-balanced to different tools.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams or track state, so signatures requiring request+response, handshake validation, and flow tracking fail - major detection blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port so bidirectional sessions are delivered intact for stateful inspection.
